title: Bermuda discount deadline Sept. 20
text:
The price to register for the 2026 Newport Bermuda Race will increase $5 per foot after Saturday, Sept. 20.
The cost for all divisions, aside from doublehanded yachts, will increase from $72 per foot to $77 following the deadline. The cost for doublehanded entries will increase from $54 per foot to $57. A deposit of 50 percent is required at registration with the balance due by April 5. Refunds will be issued to boats that cancel before Dec. 20.
The 2026 edition, which departs June 19 from Narragansett Bay, will be “one for the history books,” according to Jamestown resident Andrew Kallfelz, chairman of the event. It will be the 120th running of the race while marking the Cruising Club of America’s centennial partnership with the Royal Bermuda Yacht Club. Kallfelz said these two organizations are responsible for operating “one of the most complex and prestigious offshore events in the world.”
“Few international ocean races involve as many logistics, with a start in one country and a finish in another,” he said. “What makes it all the more remarkable? It remains a volunteer run event. … But more than the dedication of our volunteers, it’s the resilience and spirit of the sailors who step up to the challenge of this legendary 636-mile course. … When the fleet heads out of Newport bound for Bermuda, we hope to see you on the line, or cheering proudly from the shoreline, as we celebrate 100 years of partnership and a century of adventure.”
The Newport Bermuda Race, to honor this “milestone of adventure, camaraderie and seamanship,” is inviting sailors to share their most memorable moments from past races in a storytelling series called “This One Time in the Gulf Stream.”
Stories can be submitted at bermudarace.com.
“Whether it was a thrilling midnight spinnaker run, a tricky navigation call, a crew moment that kept spirits high, or even the lessons learned in tough conditions, we want to hear your stories, and see your photos, that capture the essence of what makes this race unforgettable,” organizers said.
The 120th edition also will be the first race to include mandatory inspections of keels and rudders. Organizers are telling skippers to prepare for their inspections ASAP in case intervention is needed over the winter. Addressing the integrity of this equipment before boats are launched in the spring will ensure they are compliant.
Forty-two yachts already are registered for the so-called “thrash to the Onion Patch.” That includes Boudicca, a Reichel/Pugh 66 owned by Jamestown Richard Moody, which won its class in 2024 with a corrected time of two days, 17 minutes and one second.
